      "transcript_text": "person_1 (DOCTOR) 1.32-4.50s: Good afternoon. Have a seat and we'll begin.\nperson_2 (PATIENT) 5.82-6.52s: Morning.\nperson_1 (DOCTOR) 8.55-11.18s: In your own words, what's happened?\nperson_2 (PATIENT) 11.98-15.74s: Oh, I've been dealing with skipped beats.\nperson_1 (DOCTOR) 16.96-19.92s: When did you first notice it?\nperson_2 (PATIENT) 22.01-25.81s: I've, I've had it since last Tuesday.\nperson_1 (DOCTOR) 26.33-31.86s: Okay, give me more detail on it, whatever comes to mind.\nperson_2 (PATIENT) 32.86-44.17s: Um, it sort of comes and goes. Mostly mild. Right, I've also been feeling anxious about it, for about three months.\nperson_1 (DOCTOR) 46.21-50.93s: So, any fainting, leg swelling or family history of sudden death?\nperson_2 (PATIENT) 52.79-61.72s: Um, I haven't had fainting, leg swelling or family history of sudden death, no.\nperson_1 (DOCTOR) 63.72-65.40s: Right, what about breathlessness?\nperson_2 (PATIENT) 66.99-70.65s: Not that I've noticed, no breathlessness.\nperson_1 (DOCTOR) 71.96-73.32s: Neurologically, anything strange?\nperson_2 (PATIENT) 74.85-77.90s: Oh, no, that's all normal.\nperson_1 (DOCTOR) 79.61-81.79s: Has your skin been okay?\nperson_2 (PATIENT) 82.30-83.44s: No rashes.\nperson_1 (DOCTOR) 85.41-92.22s: What medicines are you taking at the moment? It helps to be thorough at this stage.\nperson_2 (PATIENT) 93.13-98.52s: I'm on thyroxine, 75 micrograms, every morning for my thyroid.\nperson_1 (DOCTOR) 99.64-104.12s: Any relatives with health problems I should be aware of?\nperson_2 (PATIENT) 105.04-108.09s: Um, my mother has diabetes.\nperson_1 (DOCTOR) 119.19-122.43s: So, a few questions about your lifestyle now.\nperson_2 (PATIENT) 124.21-138.56s: I've never smoked. Yes, I'm a nurse on a busy ward. I share a flat with two friends. I go to the gym a couple of times a week.\nperson_1 (DOCTOR) 149.15-151.79s: Any allergies I should know about?\nperson_2 (PATIENT) 153.34-157.16s: No, none that I know of.\nperson_1 (DOCTOR) 158.04-166.90s: Do you have any medical conditions, anything you've been treated for? I ask because it helps me narrow things down.\nperson_2 (PATIENT) 171.28-179.67s: Yeah, yes, an underactive thyroid. I didn't want to make a fuss, you know.\nperson_1 (DOCTOR) 180.81-191.57s: Okay, so. Right, so an underactive thyroid is already on your record. We'll keep that in mind today. Have you had to have anything operated on?\nperson_2 (PATIENT) 193.64-201.16s: Oh, uh, I had a lump removed from my back years ago.\nperson_1 (DOCTOR) 202.64-206.56s: Let's get your blood pressure and the other basics.\nperson_1 (DOCTOR) 213.52-214.36s: One second...\nperson_1 (DOCTOR) 234.61-243.51s: Okay: pressure 122 over 74, temp 36.9 degrees, pulse is 83 beats a minute. And SpO2 98 percent on room air.\nperson_2 (PATIENT) 245.28-246.76s: Is that okay?\nperson_1 (DOCTOR) 248.82-251.88s: So, I'll come back to those numbers.\nperson_1 (DOCTOR) 253.75-256.62s: Let me have a look at you.\nperson_1 (DOCTOR) 258.03-262.16s: So, a little pressure here, tell me if it's tender.\nperson_1 (DOCTOR) 278.92-285.54s: Pulse is regular at the moment, with a couple of early beats while I listened.\nperson_1 (DOCTOR) 287.88-290.86s: Alright, all done, you can get dressed.\nperson_1 (DOCTOR) 299.43-321.11s: Okay, thinking it through, I'm honestly not certain yet. It could be benign extra heartbeats, though we should confirm, or it might be a thyroid cause. Let's book a thyroid test to look into palpitations. I want an ECG done, that's for palpitations.\nperson_2 (PATIENT) 321.99-324.27s: Mm, uh, okay.\nperson_1 (DOCTOR) 325.39-337.53s: Try cutting out caffeine for two weeks and see if the beats settle. See me again in four weeks. That's everything from me. Any other questions?\nperson_2 (PATIENT) 339.05-342.25s: So, nothing more from me, thanks.\nperson_1 (DOCTOR) 346.56-347.89s: See you then.",
